properties.name: Asics Corp
properties.about (Forest 500):
Asics Corporation was founded in 1949 in Kobe, Japan. It was incorporated twenty years later through the merger of three companies: Onitsuka, GTO and JELENK. The company has two business segments: sports product manufacture and sales; and outdoor products manufacture and sales. The sports segment is involved in the manufacture and sale of sportswear, sports shoes and equipment. This part of the business also oversees the management and delivery of products, the planning of products, and the factoring and sales support businesses. The other business segment is focused on the manufacture and sale of outdoor products through its subsidiaries, of which it has more than 50 globally. Asics Corporation employs more than 7,400 people worldwide.
Asics Corporation is among the top ten manufacturers of footwear globally and is particularly well known for its running shoes, which are marketed to both professional and amateur athletes.  The company is therefore a significant user of leather. Asics Corporation operates a number of flagship stores and the expansion of its retail network is a key strategy for the company. The company promotes its brands through participation in a number of high profile sporting events, for example through its sponsorship of major marathons and the use of Asics equipment by top sporting teams and federations on the world stage. On top of the Asics brand, the company sells fashion-oriented items under the Onitsuka Tiger brand.

properties.name: Cresud SA
properties.about (Forest 500):
Cresud SA is an agricultural company based in Argentina, involved in the production of crops, and beef and dairy cattle. As of June 2013, the company has a beef cattle stock of over 60,000 heads, which are primarily destined for the domestic Argentine market and not for export. Crop production includes soya, corn, sunflower and wheat. Soya accounts for over half of the company's total crop production, with 220,000 tons produced in 2013. Almost half of this soya was produced in Brazil, with a large amount also produced in Argentina.
Cresud SA owns almost 1 million hectares of its own land and nearly 50,000 hectares of land under lease agreements. Of this land more than 400,000 hectares is currently productive, with a further 135,000 hectares under development. Although largely based in Argentina, since 2005 the company has been expanding into other Latin American countries including Brazil, Paraguay and Bolivia. Currently, 66% of the company's land area is in Argentina, 19% in Brazil, 13% in Paraguay and 2% in Bolivia.

properties.name: DeHeus
properties.about (Forest 500):
De Heus was founded in 1911 and has grown from a regional Dutch feed manufacturer into an international conglomerate. It is now Europe's fourth largest compound animal feed producer and cites itself as a global top 15 animal feed supplier. The company has activities in over 50 countries in Europe, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa and employs 3,000 people worldwide, operating around 30 feed mills. De Heus is still owned and managed by the De Heus Family.
De Heus manufactures feed for cattle, pigs, poultry and aquaculture; it also provides customised feed for individual farms. Subsidiaries include: Koudijis Animal Nutrition, which exports feed and related products to other European countries, Middle Eastern and African markets; and Agra-Matic, an agricultural consultancy operating in the Netherlands and Poland, providing advice in a number of areas including animal husbandry, the environment, technology and planning.
De Heus has focused upon expansion outside of Europe and entered a number of markets by establishing joint ventures in countries including China, Russia, Belgium, Ethiopia and Egypt. Further examples include an agreement with Brazilian firm, Nutrifarms LTDA, signed 2012, giving De Heus access to the Brazilian pig feed market. Investments expanding the company's infrastructure outside of Europe have also intensified DeHeus' international operations. For example, in 2013, the company opened a fourth feed factory in South Africa, manufacturing feed for not only traditional livestock but also ostrich and game. De Heus is currently investing in Vietnam, looking to become one of the top five largest feed producers. In March 2015, the company announced the opening of two new factories. Construction of a seventh Vietnamese factory is underway; a project that will cost around $30 million.

properties.name: Deichmann group
properties.about (Forest 500):
Deichmann Group is a German shoe manufacturer and retailer founded in 1913 by Heinreich Deichmann. The company was established in Essen, North Rhine Westphalia, where the headquarters are still located. Currently, Deichmann Group has around 3,600 stores across 23 European countries and the USA; 1,360 stores are in Germany and over 80 in the UK. Deichmann Group is the top shoe retail company in Europe and sold around 172 million pairs of shoes worldwide in 2014. The company aims to produce fashionable shoes at affordable prices and sells shoes for men, women and children as well as accessories, including bags. The company stocks many of their own brands such as Graceland and 5th Avenue but also has collaborations with other brands, particularly in the children's sector, for example with Hello Kitty, Disney and Peppa Pig. In addition, Deichmann stores stock sports shoes from other brands, including Adidas, Fila and Pumav.
Deichmann Group began opening stores in European countries other than Germany during the early 1990s, including in the UK in 2001 and most recently in Russia in 2014. Acquisitions have also assisted brand development. In 2002, Deichmann Group bought the US chain Off Broadway Shoes, which has over 75 stores across the US, and the company has owned Rack Room Shoes since 1984. The company continues to expand its retail presence in Germany, with the planned opening of 66 new stores in the country during 2015 alongside 150 new retail branches internationally.

properties.about (Forest 500):
Granol, headquartered in São Paulo, is one of the top three soybean crushers in Brazil and is also one of the top ten exporters from the country. The company began in 1965 as a vegetable oil producer and two years later began expansion through the acquisition other companies and plants. Now with 2,000 employees, 23 warehouses, two biodiesel production plants and five soybean processing factories, Granol is the largest producer of biodiesel (and its by-product, glycerine) from soybean in Brazil and can produce 2 million tons of soybean oil per year. It currently has approximately 7,000 clients globally.
Granol's products include: biodiesel; glycerine, which is used as an ingredient in the food and pharmaceuticals ingredient; lecithin, a biodegradable food ingredient that can act as an antioxidant or stabilizer; soybean meal, which is primarily used as animal feed; and soybean oil. Most of the company's facilities are located in southern and central Brazil.

properties.name: Groupe Danone
properties.about (Forest 500):
The Danone Group was formed following the merger of BSN and Gervais Danone in 1972; however, the company's origins can be traced back to Spain, where Danone was founded in 1919 in Barcelona, specialising in yogurt products to treat intestinal disorders. The company then expanded to France and the US. BSN was founded later in 1966, and following a series of acquisitions became a top producer of mineral water, beer and baby food. Once merged, the Danone Group conducted numerous acquisitions and embarked on a global expansion, acquiring companies in Eastern Europe, Latin America, and Asia; Danone Group's first acquisition in Asia was the soy sauce and frozen food manufacturer, Amoy, in 1991.
Today the Group's portfolio is based on the company's mission to  "bring health through food to as many people as possible", with the group having divested in its operations in beer, biscuits and sauces in favour of a focus on fresh dairy products, early life nutrition, medical nutrition and water . It operates in more than 140 countries worldwide, with its top markets being France, Russia, the US and China.
Sales in the Fresh Dairy Products range account for just under 60% of the group's consolidated sales, and Danone Group ranks as the global leader in the dairy products industry worldwide. Sales in the Early Life Nutrition range make up around one fifth of the group's total sales, and Danone therefore also occupies a similarly high market share of the global baby food market, ranking in second place overall . Further to this, Danone Group is among the top five packaged food manufacturers globally.
Several forest risk commodities are relevant to Danone's operations, with the company using soya upstream in their supply chain in the form of animal feed for dairy operations as well as paper and packaging for their products. The group uses palm oil in a variety of its nutrition products, and in 2014, reported to the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil total use of 25,000 tonnes of refined palm oil or RBD palm oil and around 500 tonnes of palm kernel oil.

properties.name: Grupo Orsa
properties.about (Forest 500):
Grupo Jari, founded in 1994, is a prominent company in the forestry, paper and packaging sectors in Brazil. It claims to be one of the largest producers of corrugated cardboard packaging in Brazil and is responsible for 3% of eucalyptus pulp on the international market.
In 2010, the Group reported that it was responsible for 1.3 million hectares of forest in the Brazilian Amazon, including 545,000 hectares of native forest and 120,000 hectares authorised for plantations. The Group's native forests are located in the Vale do Jari, on the border of the states of ParÃ¡ and AmapÃ¡. According to Brazil's National Confederation of Industry (CNI), Grupo Jari is responsible for the largest area of natural forests under sustainable management in the Brazilian Amazon and is one of the country's principal producers of sawnwood. Grupo Jari produces sawn timber for the furniture and construction industries. Although it represented just 0.3% of total sawnwood production from the Brazilian Amazon in 2010, this is significant given that Brazil is the top producer of tropical sawnwood globally, responsible for 37.54% of total production from all ITTO producer countries (2007-2012). 
Jari was initially made up of three companies: Jari Celulose, Papel e Embalagens S.A.; Jari Florestal; and Ouro Verde Amazonia. In 2012, however, Jari Celulose, Papel e Embalagens S.A. and US-based firm, International Paper, formed a joint corrugated packaging venture: Orsa International Paper Embalagens S.A. Having originally owned 75% of the joint venture, International Paper acquired the remainder in 2014 and is therefore is now in charge of Jari Celulose's packaging assets. Groupo Jari also partners with a number of companies manufacturing construction materials, such as wooden decks and flooring, for overseas retailers.

properties.about (Forest 500):
Founded in Hong Kong in the 1800s, CK Hutchison Holdings Ltd (CK Hutchison) operates five core businesses: ports and related services, retail, infrastructure, energy and telecommunication. The company was formed in its present structure in 2015 following the restructuring of Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd. and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd. to separate the property business into a new holding company and subsume Hutchison Whampoa's other operations under the direction of CK Hutchison. CK Hutchison employs around 270,000 people across 50 countries.
CK Hutchison's retail operations are led by A.S. Watson Group, which was started in 1828 as a small dispensary in Guangzhou, China. Today, the Group has more than 12,000 stores in 22 countries worldwide and claims to be the world's largest international health and beauty retailer. The company operates multiple brands in the health and beauty sector, including: Watsons, which has over 4,800 stores and 1,400 pharmacies in Asia and Europe; Kruidvat, which has over 1,000 stores in the Netherlands and Belgium; and Superdrug, which operates in the UK and Ireland and has over 870 stores. A.S. Watson also sells food, wine and electronics under multiple brands, which include: PARKnSHOP, which operates 340 supermarkets in Greater China; and SU-PA-DE-PA, which combines supermarket food products with department store ranges, such as clothing and entertainment. The Group's portfolio also includes over 500 European perfume and cosmetics shops.

properties.name: Inditex SA
properties.sectors: Apparel & footwear; Accessories & luggage; Furniture & flooring
properties.about (Forest 500):
Inditex SA owns the clothing and accessories retail brands Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius, Oysho, Uterque and Zara Home. This Spanish company, formed by Amancio Ortega Gaona in 1963, is amongst the largest fashion retailers in the world, with a revenue of over €16 billion 2013.
Inditex SA started business with Zara in 1963, which is the largest and best known of all the company's brands; selling leather shoes and handbags, as well as mid-range clothes to men, women and children. Inditex was incorporated as the group's holding company in 1985 and in 1991 other brands were incorporated into the group. Today, Inditex has more than 6,000 stores in 88 countries around the world, with recent expansions into China and Russia. Outside of Zara, its other brands cover a wide range of markets, for example, Uterque is a dedicated accessory store, and Berksha and Pull&Bear target younger audiences.
Almost 90% of Inditex' suppliers come from Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Turkey, India, South East Asia, Bangladesh, China, Brazil and Argentina, with over half of the company's manufacturing taking place in Spain or nearby countries, including Turkey and Morocco. This allows the company to respond to in-store demands and trends quickly, a model that has been dubbed 'Fast Fashion'. The company sells a range of apparel and accessories, including leather products, and notably, ranks in the top ten footwear companies in the western European market.

properties.name: Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group Co Ltd
properties.about (Forest 500):
Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group Co Ltd (Yili Group) is a packaged food manufacturer, specialising in the production of dairy products. Its principal products include milk and other dairy-based foods, and can be classified into five major business divisions: liquid milk, powdered milk, ice cream, yogurt; and raw milk. As well as these, the company's products include other frozen foods, noodles, cheese, and soya bean powder. In total Yili Group has around 100 subsidiary companies and manufactures over 1000 products.
Since it was founded in Hohhot, China, in 1956, the company has established itself as a key player in the global packaged food industry. In 1993 the company was restructured as a group of companies under its current name and in 2005 it became China's leading company in the supply of milk powder and milk tea powder. Today, it ranks as both the top dairy and packaged food company on the Chinese market, and is among the top 20 packaged food companies overall worldwide. Furthermore, being listed on the Forbes 2000, it is also among the top public companies in the world.
Palm oil is commonly used as a base oil in ice cream, making it the most relevant forest risk commodity to Yili Group's operations. The Chinese ice cream industry consumed over 110,000 tonnes of palm oil in 2011. Yili holds the leading market share in the Chinese ice cream market, with its ice cream products including the Chocliz and Yili Pastureland brands.

properties.about (Forest 500):
JVL Agro Industries Ltd (JVL), formally Jhunjhunwala Vanaspati Limited, is an Indian edible oil manufacturer. The company was incorporated in 1989, and was established initially in Northern India as a manufacturer of hydrogenated vegetable oils and refined oils, with the capacity to produce around 25 tonnes per day. The company has since grown to be the largest vegetable oil manufacturer in the country, with four plants producing 300 tonnes a day, with products including palm oil and soya bean oil.
The company's mid- and downstream activities require a large amount of raw material, therefore JVL are responsible for around 5% of India's total crude palm oil imports. JVL is also taking steps to acquire new land in Indonesia and Ethiopia for the production of palm oil and, as of 2013, had signed an agreement for the use of 12,500 acres of land in Ethiopia, with the potential of extending this to 62,000 acres.
JVL has a number of brands under which products are distributed to the consumer market across 18 Indian states. For example, refined soya bean oil is sold under the Jhoola health brand, while blended oils are sold under the Joohi active brand. JVL are working towards the development of rapid revenue growth partly by diversifying into new markets. For example, in 2012, they began to market bakery products, and in 2013-14 were set to commission a rice mill in Bihar with a production capacity of 12 metric tonnes per hour.

properties.name: Kellogg Co
properties.about (Forest 500):
Kellogg Co was originally established in 1906 as the Battle Creek Toasted Corn Flake Company. They are now the world's largest cereal company, manufacturing around 1,600 products in 18 countries, and marketing these in more than 180 countries worldwide. Aside from their cereal products, Kellogg Co also manufactures a number of snacks and frozen foods, including crisps, ready-meals, meat alternatives and biscuits. These products are sold through several well-known brands including Kellogg's, Fruit loops, Kashi, Pringles and Keebler. Despite already operating a number of manufacturing facilities across the globe, Kellogg Co continues to expand its supply chain into new areas. Notably, the company is building a new facility in Malaysia to take advantage of the rapidly growing Asia Pacific market.  This facility, due to be operational from mid-2015, is set to produce halal Pringles and other snacks, and will create over 300 jobs. In total, they currently operate manufacturing, distribution and warehouse facilities totalling more than 35 million square feet, both in the US and internationally.
As a major manufacturer of packaged food, Kellogg Co uses both soya and palm oil. For example, palm oil is used in a variety of the company's branded products, such as in its cookies and waffles, and soya is used in cereal, such as in Kellogg's Smart Start Soy Protein.

properties.name: Kering SA
properties.about (Forest 500):
Kering SA is a French company engaged in the retail and distribution of luxury goods, primarily apparel and accessories. Until 2013, the company was known as PPR, short for Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, which in turn was its official name until 2005.  Established in 1963, the company has its origins in the building materials industry and in particular in the timber trade. It then became a leader in the retail sector, before entering into the world of luxury goods with the purchase of the Gucci brand in 1999. Today the company has 22 brands operating in two core divisions: Luxury, which designs, manufactures and markets luxury apparel, leather goods, accessories, watches, jewellery, fragrances and cosmetics; and Sport and Lifestyle, which designs and produces footwear, apparel and accessories under the company's sporting brands.
Kering SA is headquartered in Paris, France and its brands in its luxury and sports and lifestyle segments, include several world famous brands including Puma, Saint Laurent, Alexander McQueen, Balenciaga and Stella McCartney, many of which have leather goods among their principal products,. Kering SA therefore plays a prominent role in the global trade in leather and animal skins, with several of the company's brands designing and selling leather goods. For example, it produces leather wallets and handbags under Saint Laurent  and Balenciaga. Through these and its numerous other brands, Kering SA holds the second largest market share in the bags and luggage sector globally. It also produces large amount s of leather footwear, for example under Sergio Rossi; a leading Italian shoe brand. Kering SA is among the top five manufacturers of footwear globally, occupying the fourth largest share of the global market in 2013, and in particular holding a leading position in the footwear market of Western Europe, especially in Italy. Kering SA is placing increasing emphasis on the direct sourcing of its raw materials, including leather. In 2013, it bought a majority stake in one the world's biggest producers of tanned skins and it has plans to build a new tanning facility in France, which could be operational by 2016.

properties.name: Kikkoman Corp
properties.about (Forest 500):
Kikkoman Corporation (Kikkoman) is a holding company concerned with the manufacture of food, mainly soy sauce and alcohols. It is a Japanese company and was founded in 1917, though its website claims its soy sauce manufacturing history dates back a further 200 years. Aside from soy sauce, the company also produces related seasonings and drinks (mainly alcoholic); it also produces enzymes and other biochemical products. There are 67 companies in the group and it has a total of 5,622 employees.
There are four segments to the business. The domestic food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce and soya related seasonings, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, as well as cans, soya milk drinks and health food products. The domestic 'other products' segment includes drugs, chemicals, real estate, logistic and indirect services. The overseas food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, cans, soya milk drinks and health food products, in overseas markets. Finally, the overseas food wholesales segment purchases and sells oriental food products.
Outside of Japan, Kikkoman produces soy sauce in the US, Europe, Singapore and Taiwan. It is the largest sauce, dressings and condiments company in Japan, the second largest in Hong Kong for canned and preserved food, and one of the top ten largest sauce, dressings and condiments manufacturers in the World.

properties.name: Kimberly-Clark
properties.sectors: Personal care; Personal care; Paper & packaging
properties.about (Forest 500):
Kimberly-Clark Group, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, in the US, is a leading international company in the personal care, health and hygiene industry. It has a long history in supplying paper products for personal care, having been founded over 140 years ago in the state of Wisconsin in the US in 1870. The company produces feminine, adult, family, baby and child care products, as well as products for the professional and health care sectors, including diapers, facial and bathroom tissue, and paper towels. Its well-known brands include Kleenex, which was the world's pioneering facial tissue, and Huggies, a leading brand of diaper that is central to the company's multi-billion dollar baby-care business. It is the leading company in the retail tissue industry globally, and also occupies the second place amongst the top 100 forestry, paper and packaging companies globally, ranked by sales, in 2013.
The company has manufacturing facilities in 37 countries, including in India, Indonesia, Brazil, China and the Republic of Korea and its brands are sold in 175 countries worldwide. properties.name: Kingfisher PLC
properties.about (Forest 500):
Kingfisher PLC (Kingfisher) is a home improvement company, operating chains of retail stores. Kingfisher is based in the UK and though its domestic market dominates its operations, it is also active overseas, with a presence throughout Europe and in China. 
The company is Europe's leading retailer in the DIY sector and it is the third largest globally. Kingfisher's operations date back to 1982, with the acquisition of FW Woolworth, with which came a small chain of B&Q DIY retail outlets. B&Q is now one of Kingfisher's main retail brands, along with Castorama, Brico Dept, Screwfix, and Koçta?. B&Q supplies DIY and garden products and stocks a number of wooden products, including garden sheds and indoor and outdoor furniture, wooden flooring, and construction, finishing and decorative timber. It has over 350 stores in the UK and Ireland, and 39 in China. B&Q opened its first stores in China in 1999, however after some initial problems in entering the market the company scaled back and restructured its operations to better adapt to the Chinese market, involving a focus on the local preference for 'Do-it-for-me' rather than the traditional 'Do-it-yourself' (DIY), which has stabilised its position as a leader in the somewhat fragmented market. 
Castorama is similarly a chain of home and garden stores, with over 100 outlets in France, 72 stores in Poland, and 20 in Russia. Brico Dept is a more specialist chain of stores, providing products for professional builders and more experienced consumers. The majority of Brico Dept's business is in France, where it has over 100 stores, but it also has stores in Spain and Romania. Screwfix has stores in the UK and provides tools and hardware products. Finally, Koçta? is Turkey's leading home improvement retailer, with 46 stores.

properties.about (Forest 500):
LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SA (LVMH) is a French company, with its headquarters in Paris, engaged in the luxury goods industry. The group was formed following the merger of the MoÃ«t Hennessy and Louis Vuitton companies in 1987; however its origins extend back much further in the history of the development of the French luxury goods industry. Louis Vuitton's flagship brand was launched in 1854, after which it continued to specialise solely in handmade leather bags for over 70 years, while, Moet Hennessy's origins are even earlier, as the company was involved in the wine industry for 100 years prior.
LVMH currently operates in five main segments: wines and spirits; fashion and leather goods; perfumes and cosmetics; watches and jewellery; and selective retailing. Within these five sectors, LVMH has a portfolio of more than 60 brands and an international network of more than 3,000 stores. Of particular importance is the company's fashion and leather goods division, which comprises well-known luggage, leather goods and apparel and accessories brands, such as Louis Vuitton, Givenchy and Marc Jacobs.
In 2013, the fashion and leather goods business accounted for the majority of the group's total revenue. The group is an industry leader in the bags and luggage market worldwide, occupying the top position globally in terms of market share and leading positions in the individual markets of China, Western Europe and the USA.

properties.name: Lactalis Groupe
properties.about (Forest 500):
Groupe Lactalis is a French company specialising in dairy products, including milk powder and nutrition products, cheese, liquid milk, fats and chilled dairy goods. The company, originally known as Societe Laitiere Besnier, was established in 1939 and changed its name to Groupe Lactalis S.A. in 1999. Visible in 150 countries and with on the ground operations in 70 countries (as of 2011), Lactalis has grown to have a global presence and ranks itself the world's leading dairy group. The company employs around 61,000 people and operates a total of 200 industrial plants.  The majority of its operations are in Europe, where it employs almost 40,000 people, however it is active worldwide, with operations in America, Africa and Asia/Oceania.  In September 2014, the Group, through its Parmalat subsidiary, agreed to buy the dairy units of Brazilian food company BRF, and has also agreed to buy units of Brazilian dairy company, LBR-Lacteos (which previously held license to use the Parmalat brand name in Brazil).
The group's branded products include President cheese, Rachel's yoghurt, Roquefort Socieite and Munch Bunch. It also has a long history with Nestle and took over a subsidiary, Claudel Roustang, in 1985. In 2006 Groupe Lactalis and Nestle created a subsidiary, Lactalis Nestle, which deals with Nestle's fresh dairy produce and owns yoghurt brands, Munch Bunch and Ski, in the UK. In addition to its recognisable dairy brands, Groupe Lactalis also provides ingredients for industry, including whey products, lactose and milk powder, to be used in the manufacture of products such as ice-cream, ready meals and confectionery.
Groupe Lactalis also uses palm oil in some of its products. For example, its Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division, produces butters, creams and margarines, some of which contain palm oil, as do the products of the Lactalis Nutrition Sante division. The Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division does not currently measure how much palm oil it uses but it plans to start sourcing RSPO-certified oil palm products in 2015 and to be using 100% RSPO-certified oil palm by 2018 (on own-brand products). properties.name: Land O'Lakes Purina
properties.about (Forest 500):
Land O'Lakes Inc. is one of America's largest cooperatives, employing 9,000 people and with 3,200 producer-members and 1,000 member-cooperatives serving over 300,000 agricultural producers. In 2013 it had annual sales of $14.2 billion, and it ranks #194 on the Fortune 500. The company has four business segments: dairy foods, crop inputs, animal feed and business services. Dairy foods products are provided by its Dairy Foods and Kozy Shack businesses. Crop inputs are provided by its Winfield Solutions business, and its animal feeds are provided by its Purina Animal Nutrition LLC, Land O'Lakes Feed LLC and Purina Mills LLC businesses.
Dairy Foods sells mainly butter and cheese, under the under the Land O Lakes and Alpine Lace brands. It claims to produce America's #1 brand of butter and deli american cheese. The Land O Lakes brand is also licensed to a small number of partner companies who produce milk, creams, juices, eggs, cottage cheese, sour cream, yogurt and cocoa mixes, such as the WhiteWaves Food Company. Kozy Shack, acquired in 2012, produces chilled desserts such as rice pudding, tapioca pudding and flans and claims to be America's #1 brand of tapioca and rice pudding.
Purina Animal Nutrition LLC provides supplements, ingredients, complete feeds and speciality technologies to farmers and the consumer (pet) markets via several thousand local cooperatives, independent dealers and other retailers in the US. The company is heavily involved in research and development and has over 100 patents worldwide. Land O'Lakes Inc. animal feed production began with feed for mules and horses in 1894, and today its feed products are produced for an extremely broad range of animals from farm animals, during multiple lifecycle stages, to fish, pets and exotic animals. Land O'Lakes Inc. is one of the world's top five largest animal feed producers and therefore purchases large quantities of soya, some of which is used in animal feed production,. As some animal feeds also use palm oil, Land O'Lakes Inc. may also source palm oil for use as an ingredient.
Land O'Lakes Inc. is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil or the Roundtable on Responsible Soy.

properties.about (Forest 500):
Lindt & Sprungli AG (Lindt) is a Swiss chocolatier founded in 1845, which describes itself as the market leader in the premium chocolates industry. The company sells in over 100 countries worldwide, with products under the brand names Ghirardelli, Caffarel, Hofbauer and Kufferle. Lindt employs a total of 8,949 people, has eight production sites (six in Europe and two in the USA) and distributes globally (including in China, Australia, South Africa, North America and Europe), with its largest markets being the European and NAFTA countries. The company distributes its products through a variety of avenues, including duty free retail outlets in airports, department stores, its own stores and Chocolate Cafes.
As a confectionery company, Lindt is ranked 7th in the world and 6th in Western Europe, and is also ranked among the top 50 packaged food companies globally. Further to this, Lindt is placed among the Forbes Global 2000 list. As a manufacturer of sweet snacks, Lindt uses palm oil in a number of its products and also includes soya derivatives, such as soya lecithin, as an ingredient in most of its chocolates.
Lindt has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2008. In 2012 it used 2,565m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products; and it aims to be sourcing 100% RSPO-certified sustainable palm oil by 2015.

properties.about (Forest 500):
Mars Inc. (Mars) is a global leader in the confectionery industry, and also a significant player in the market for dried processed foods, sauces and condiments. The company was originally founded in 1891, and has its origins in the confectionery business, for which it remains most well-known. Headquartered in the state of Virginia in the US, Mars is the third largest private company in the America and employs over 65,000 'associates.' These associates work in 230 locations and factories in 68 countries worldwide. The company's operations are divided between six divisions: pet care products, chocolate, a variety of packaged food, chewing gum and candy under the Wrigley business segment, drinks and finally, scientific research under Mars Symbioscience.
Mars manufactures goods under numerous well-known global brands, including ready meal brands, Uncle Ben's and Suzi Wan, and chocolates brands including Maltesers, Bounty, Galaxy, M&Ms, Twix, Snickers and many more.  Mars sources a variety of raw materials to manufacture its diverse product range. Several forest risk commodities are among these, including beef, which comprises 3.6% of Mars' raw materials purchased by volume, as well as palm oil, soya and pulp and paper. In 2012/2013, Mars reported use of over 77,000 tonnes of palm oil, making its palm oil consumption higher than many other manufacturers.
Mars continues to increase its manufacturing capacity, opening a new $270 million chocolate plant in Kansas, America.  The company is also aiming to improve its market position in petcare through the planned acquisition of the IAMS, Eukanuba and Natura brands from Procter and Gamble for $2.9 billion. properties.name: Meiji Holdings
properties.about (Forest 500):
Meiji Holdings Co. Ltd. (Meiji Holdings) is a Japanese holding company, headquartered in Tokyo, that through its subsidiaries has operations in the manufacture of dairy products, confectionery, health food and pharmaceuticals. The company, in its current holding company structure, was established in 2008; however, its origins extend back to the early 1900s, with the establishment of Meiji Sugar Co. Ltd. and Meiji Dairies Corporation in 1906, and then Meiji Co. Ltd. (a manufacturer of confectionery) in 1916.  
Meiji Holdings' business activities now fall under Meiji Co. Ltd. and Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd. Meiji Co. Ltd. produces a variety of food products, under its confectionery, dairy, healthcare & nutritionals, and international business units. Whereas Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd manufactures pharmaceuticals in three main segments: anti-infective drugs, therapeutic drugs for neural disorders, and generic drugs. The company is active within Japan and internationally, through its overseas network of companies, which can be found throughout Asia, Europe and North America. Meiji Holdings ranks among the top 2,000 public companies in the world and has over 14,000 employees.
The company's operations in packaged food manufacturing, in particular its use of palm and soya products in the production of sweets, chocolate and ice cream, are of particular importance with respect to forest risk commodities. For example, palm oil and palm kernel oil can be found in Meiji's brands of chocolate cookies and crackers, Chococones and Chocorooms, which it markets in the United States. Similarly, palm oil and soya derivatives can be found in other products, such as Meiji's Apollo Strawberry Chocolate Candy.
Meiji Holdings is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

properties.about (Forest 500):
Mitsubishi Corp is a core company of the Mitsubishi Group; a group of autonomous companies made up of about 28 core enterprises and up to 600 member companies in all. The companies within the Mitsubishi Group conduct their operations independently of one another, but each honour the Group's three principles (of corporate social responsibility; integrity and fairness; and global understanding through business) and have their roots in the original shipping company, founded in 1870.
Mitsubishi Corp is a general trading company; the largest in Japan and the largest publicly-listed company of its kind in the world. The company's history extends back to 1954, when the Mitsubishi Shoji was established; however, Mitsubishi Corporation became the company's official English name in 1971. Mitsubishi Corp's activities now expand well beyond its original trading operations and it is involved in a wide variety of businesses, including energy, metals, food and environmental business.  Of particular relevance are Mitsubishi's operations in the production of food products that include soya and palm-based ingredients. Significantly, the Living Essentials department of Mitsubishi Corp also operates as a trading company in the palm oil industry, where it purchases predominantly Malaysian palm oil for export to Japan, the US and Taiwan, among others. The Living Essentials Group's activities in the production of consumer goods also include the procurement of raw materials and the manufacturing and distribution of a wide variety of products, including furniture, lumber, housing and construction materials, as well as many processed and frozen foods.
Mitsubishi Corp acquired UK-based food and drink manufacturer, Princes Ltd., in 1989. This is another particularly relevant component of Mitsubishi's operations. Founded in Liverpool, UK in 1880, Princes has since greatly increased its business portfolio diversifying from its original focus on the sale of canned goods. With a total of 19 mergers and acquisitions, it is now among the top food and drinks manufacturers in the UK.  Its tinned and canned products include meat pies, corned beef and stewed steak and the company is among the top five European beef importers from Brazil.

properties.name: News Corporation
properties.about (Forest 500):
News Corporation (News Corp) is a media conglomerate with a network of companies in media, news, education and information services. In June 2013, News Corp's shareholders gave formal approval for the company to split its publishing and entertainment divisions, creating two new companies: News Corp, housing the company's publishing segment; 21st Century Fox housing the entertainment division. News Corp is now specifically a publishing company, producing newspaper, magazines, books and promotional inserts and coupons. The company was established in Australia in 1954, when Rupert Murdoch took control of the Australian corporation, News Limited, which had a majority interest in one of Adelaide's top daily newspapers. Since then, the company has grown dramatically and acquired numerous assets, beginning with newspapers in the UK: 'The Sun' and 'News of the World.' Established in Australia, News Corp is now based in the US and is the largest newspaper publishing company globally.
As of 2014, News Corp is comprised of the following businesses, with each housing several brands: News Corp Australia, News UK, Dow Jones & Company, New York Post, Harper Collins Publishers, Amplify, News America Marketing, and Storyful. News Corp Australia, for example, claims to be Australia's leading media and publishing company, selling over 10 million papers weekly, with titles including The Daily Telegraph, The Australian, and Herald Sun. News UK also publishes some of the UK's most well-known newspapers, including The Sun, The Times and The Sunday Times. Dow Jones & Company publishes The Wall Street Journal and specialises in the provision of news and business information via a variety of media outlets.  Finally, News Corp's subsidiary HarperCollins is one of the world's most prominent book publishing companies. In May 2014, HarperCollins acquired book publisher Harlequin; the acquisition of the Canadian company is the biggest deal in book publishing since the merger of two other publishing giants, Penguin and Random House in 2013.

properties.name: Nike Inc
properties.about (Forest 500):
Nike Inc. was incorporated in 1969, and has grown to become the largest manufacturer of footwear in the world; it also claims to be one of the world's largest users of white leather for footwear.
Nike Inc. focuses on the design, development, and marketing of athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, and accessory products, and sells its products worldwide to retail stores as well as through its own subsidiaries and distributors. It has five key brands: Nike, Converse, Hurley, Jordan and Nike Golf and in 2013, Nike ranked among the world's 25 most valuable brands. Nike Inc's subsidiary, Converse, also designs, distributes and licenses athletic and casual footwear as well as apparel under trademarks that include Converse, Chuck Taylor, All Star, One Star, Star Chevron and Jack Purcell.
Nearly all of Nike Inc's footwear is manufactured outside of the United States by independent contract manufacturers. Most of these are based in Vietnam, China and Indonesia, which together account for 8% of the Nike brand footwear. Apparel is produced in 28 countries including China, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Malaysia, Turkey, Mexico and Cambodia. Globally, nearly 50,000 people work for Nike Inc. including in the 750 company-owned and operated retail stores.

properties.name: Nisshin OilliO Group Ltd
properties.about (Forest 500):
The Nisshin OilliO Group Ltd (Nisshin OilliO) is a Japanese company involved in the processing and manufacturing of oils and oil-based products. Established in 1907, it claims to be the largest vegetable oil company in Japan and today operates a number of companies involved in the manufacture, processing and distribution of manufactured goods, including oils, fats and chemical products. Its main business segments are: Oils and Meals; Processed Oils and Fats; Healthy Foods; Fine Chemicals; and Soya Foods and Materials. Nisshin OilliO's main oil-based products include: edible oils for household and commercial use, and food processing; margarines, shortenings, and other processed and speciality oils and fats; healthy oil products, premium oils and soya bean oil; and finally, dressings, and other healthy food products. However, its business operations also extend to a variety of other sectors, with the group also active in the insurance, marketing and restaurant industries, among others.
The Nisshin OilliO Group has four manufacturing facilities in Japan, as well as overseas subsidiaries in China, Taiwan, Malaysia, Singapore, Europe and North America. In 2005, the Group acquired Malaysian company, Intercontinental Speciality Fats Sdn. Bhd (ISF), an edible oils and fats manufacturer, supplying products for the chocolate and confectionery, bakery, dairy, and convenience food industries. ISF operates two refineries in Malaysia , where it occupies a 5% of the oil palm refinery market.

properties.name: Nitori Holdings Co., Ltd.
properties.about (Forest 500):
Nitori Holdings Co Ltd is a furniture company based in Hokkaido, Japan. The company dates back to 1967 when it opened its first furniture store and in 2010 the company was restructured: Nitori Holdings Co Ltd was established, marking the transition of Nitori Co Ltd to a holding company structure whereby Nitori Holdings Co Ltd oversees the Nitori group of companies,.The company operates a chain of furniture stores, and sells its own brand, manufactured as well as imported merchandise. It is the largest home furnishings company in Japan and the third largest globally. As a manufacturer and retailer of furniture and interior products, the company has operations at multiple stages of the supply chain.
Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is the manufacturing arm of the Nitori group and produces a variety of furniture products, including cupboards, beds, and kitchen storage units. Nitori Furniture Co Ltd sources raw materials from around the world and has procurement facilities in seven countries, including in China, Malaysia and Thailand. Around 80% of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are sourced from overseas and as part of its expansion outside of Japan, the company also supports the operations of two furniture factories in Indonesia (since 1994) and Vietnam (since 2004). Some of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are manufactured at externally-owned facilities; however, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd maintains close contact with and involvement in all its business operations through the establishment of regional offices. Furthermore, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is directly responsible for the import and distribution of all products to its stores, with its subsidiary Home Logistics Co Ltd responsible for all domestic distribution.
In terms of the group's retail activities, Nitori Co Ltd operates over 300 stores, both in Japan and abroad. Although the group was originally inspired by the developed furniture and home interiors markets of the United States and Europe, Nitori Co Ltd's growth is well demonstrated by its entrance into the US market, where in 2013, it opened its first store under the Aki-Home brand in California.

properties.name: Pearson plc
properties.about (Forest 500):
Pearson Plc (Pearson) is a London-based international media and education company, with key operations in the publishing industry. The company develops and publishes educational and entertainment materials in the form of books, newspapers and online. Pearson provides educational materials to teachers and students across 70 countries.  It also runs the Financial Times Group, a leading provider of business and financial news and analysis, both in print and online. Finally, Pearson is also the parent company of Penguin Random House, which claims to be the first truly global trade book publisher, and comprises the various publishing enterprises of the previously separate Penguin and Random House companies. Penguin Random House was formed in July 2013 after a merger was agreed between the respective publishing enterprises' parent companies, Pearson and Bertelsmann. The joint venture is based in New York and is jointly controlled by the two companies, with 53% owned by Bertelsmann, based in Germany, and 47% by Pearson.
In 2013, the book publishing operations of Pearson, the Penguin Group and Penguin Random House, individually ranked as the top two players in the book publishing industry globally. Only a very small proportion of Pearson's products are printed in-house, with the company instead sourcing from a number of suppliers around the world. For example, commercial printing company R. R. Donnelley, which is the leading company of its kind globally in terms of market share, is an important supplier of Pearson.

It is headquartered in Illinois, USA and provides a range of communication services to corporate customers, enabling them disperse messages using various types of media. Despite offering a number of digital communication strategies, they are primarily known as a supplier of print material and is the leading company of its kind globally.  R. R. For example, it supplies print products to Pearson PLC and to HarperCollins, two of the world's largest publishers. In 2013 it employed roughly 57,000 people across four continents, in nearly 40 countries, leading to sales of $10.5 billion. It continues to expand through strategic acquisitions of companies specialising in both digital and commercial print. For example, in 2011, it acquired LibreDigital, a pioneering digital publishing and distribution company, and in 2014 acquired Consolidated Graphics in a deal worth over $600 million.

properties.name: Rezervnaja Prodovol'stvennaja Kompanija
properties.about (Forest 500):
According to figures on imports of beef to Russia, Rezervnaja Prodovol'stvennaja Kompanija TD ZAO (Reserve Food Company), is among the top importers of beef products from Latin America, accounting for around 32,000 tons of frozen beef imports from Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay in 2013. The company is a closed joint stock company (ZAO) based in Moscow and founded in October 2002.  It is a meat wholesaler, offering a variety of meat products, including livestock, poultry and offal and is a member of Russia's National Meat Association.
According to Kontragent, an official database on Russian legal entities, in 2012, Reserve Food Company made net profit of 145,000 million RUB (343 million USD), that is 25 million RUB or 13% less than the previous year, likely due to an increase in the cost of products.

properties.name: Rimbunan Hijau
properties.about (Forest 500):
Rimbunan Hijau Group (RH Group) is among Malaysia's largest conglomerates. The group operates in a variety of sectors including forestry, oil palm, media, information communication technologies and hospitality, and also holds diverse business interests, such as aquaculture and mining. RH Group's operations are found internationally, including in Cambodia, China, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Singapore and the US. The group is complex in structure, with numerous publicly-listed and privately-held subsidiaries operating under various holding companies.
RH Group is a key player in the international timber industry, involved in forestry and the processing and manufacturing of timber products. It is one of the two largest forestry enterprises in Malaysia, where it has extensive concessions in Sarawak of over 1 million hectares. These include the concessions of subsidiary Jaya Tiasa Holdings Berhad, which comprises about 12% of Sarawak's production forest. It also claims to be the largest veneer and plywood manufacturer in the country, accounting for 10% of total production.
RH Group is also involved in timber processing in Africa, China, Papua New Guinea, and outside of the tropics in Russia and New Zealand. In Gabon, RH Group manages the largest forestry enterprise, with a total area of over 900,000 hectares. The group also plays a central role in timber trade between Africa and China. For example, it has been reported that almost all timber from the Republic of Congo is exported through RH Group , with the majority destined for the Chinese market.
Under Rimbunan Hijau (PNG) Limited, RH Group dominates the forestry industry in Papua New Guinea (PNG), where it is responsible for about one third of all PNG's log exports. RH Group has timber processing and manufacturing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer and plywood, primarily for the export market. The group also owns one of PNG's two major newspapers: The National, and is one of the country's largest employers in the private sector.
RH Group is also active in the palm oil sector. Its subsidiary, investment holding company Rimbunan Sawit Berhad (RSB) is a key player in the industry in Sarawak and has several subsidiaries with plantation and processing operations. RSB has around 93,500 hectares of plantations in Sarawak and one mill, with a second expected to be commissioned in 2015. Further to this, RH Group has about 31,000 hectares allocated for oil palm development in East New Britain in PNG.

properties.name: Saint Gobain SA
properties.about (Forest 500):
Saint-Gobain SA is a multinational corporation that manufactures and distributes construction materials.  Established in France in 1665 as the first company to produce glass on an industrial scale, Saint-Gobain has a long history in the sector and is now a leading company in the distribution of building materials. Specifically, it is among the top five industry leaders in Europe's increasingly consolidated building products distribution sector. Saint-Gobain claims to be the largest of these industry players; with over 4,000 sales outlets and over 17,000 employees in the manufacturing and distribution sectors in the UK and Ireland alone.
Saint-Gobain houses several enterprises in the construction and building materials distribution industries. The company's construction products activities include the production of cast iron pipe systems, plasterboard and plaster products, insulation, industrial mortars and exterior products. Saint-Gobain's building distribution activities operate under several trading brands in 27 countries, including 16 brands in France, 12 in Germany and 18 in the UK.
International Timber is one of Saint-Gobain's brands in the UK, supplying timber and timber products to a range of industry sectors.  International Timber produces a variety of wood products, including hardwoods, softwoods, decking, flooring and engineered timber components. The company imports tropical sawnwood from South America, including from Brazil; from West Africa, including Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo; and from Asia, including Indonesia. Another of Saint-Gobain's subsidiaries in the UK is Jewson. Jewson is the UK's leading supplier of building materials and timber products, which it sources from International Timber.

properties.name: Samko Timber
properties.about (Forest 500):
Samko Timber Ltd is a forest products company listed in Singapore and based in Indonesia. It produces a variety of timber products, including plywood, decking, doors, window frames, piano parts, laminated veneer lumber, laminated veneer board, and truck body parts. One of the largest and well established logging and plywood companies in Indonesia, the company was founded in 1978 and has since become a major player in the processed timber products industry in Indonesia; it also claims to be among the top five tropical hardwood producers in the world.
Samko Timber Ltd has numerous subsidiaries, with the majority of its operations in Indonesia. For example, Bioforest Pte Ltd is based in Singapore but its 99.9% owned subsidiary, PT Bioforest Indonesia is based and operates in Indonesia. Similarly, Samko Trading Pte Ltd, based in Singapore, has operations through its 100% owned subsidiaries in Indonesia and Malaysia (Samkowood Product Sdn Bhd). On top of its activities in Southeast Asia, Samko Timber Ltd has established a joint venture in the US under Samko USA LLC, to market its products in North America. 
Within Indonesia, the company has procurement, processing, manufacturing and distribution operations. Specifically, Samko Timber Ltd has five processing units in Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi; ten veneer plants in Java and Sumatra; a 9,400 hectare industrial tree plantation in Jambi, Sumatra; and through its associate company, in Kalimantan it has 4 forest plantations of 125,000 hectares and four natural forest logging concessions covering a total of 450,000 hectares.

properties.name: Samsonite International
properties.about (Forest 500):
Samsonite International SA is a US based luggage company involved in the design, manufacturing, marketing and sale of luggage and travel accessories. Its products include luggage, business accessories, such as laptop cases, and outdoor and casual bags. The company was established in 1910 in the state of Colorado, and has since grown to be a leader in the luggage and bags industry; manufacturing products under multiple brands and selling them worldwide.
The company's products are sold under several brands, including Samsonite, American Tourister, High Sierra, Hartmann, Lipault, and Speck, as well as other owned and licensed brand names. Samsonite International claims to be the largest travel luggage company in the world, and in 2013 sold its products through over 46,000 sales points in more than 100 countries worldwide. The company is one of the few luggage groups to sell its products across the globe, in North America, Europe, Latin America, and throughout Asia, including India and China. In 2012, at 12%, Samsonite International occupied the largest market share in the global luggage industry, making it three times larger than its closest competitor.  Several of Samsonite International's brands produce leather products, such as the Business Leather line under the Samsonite brand, as well as business cases, tote bags and other leather accessories under the Hartmann brand.
Samsonite's products are predominantly manufactured in Asia. The company outsources around 94% of its manufacturing, with manufacturing facilities in China producing up to 84% of the total, and the rest produced throughout Asia, predominantly in Vietnam, India, Bangladesh and Thailand.

properties.about (Forest 500):
Japan based Seven & I Holdings Co Ltd (Seven & I Holdings) is a holding company that established from the merger of Ito-Yokado Co, Seven Eleven Japan Co, and Denny's Japan. Through its subsidiaries, Seven & I Holdings operates convenience stores, food supermarkets, department stores, general merchandise stores, food services, financial services and IT services.
As of 2014, there were around 56,000 Seven & I Holdings stores in 16 different countries in Asia, Scandinavia, the Americas and Australia, serving, on average, 58 million customers per day, 20.5 million of which were in Japan. The bulk of the portfolio is made up of over 56,600 7-Eleven convenience stores, the world's largest franchise chain store. In addition to the 7-Eleven banner Seven & I Holdings operate Sogo & Seibu department stores; several hundred food supermarkets under the York Mart and York-Benimaru banners; superstores predominantly using the Ito Yokado banner; a number of speciality stores; and restaurants, including around 470 Denny's restaurants in Japan. Seven & I Holdings also have a number of consumer financial services subsidiaries. Within the food sector, Seven & I subsidiaries have a number of own or private brand labels including 7-Select, Seven Premium and Seven Gold; these brands include meat products, baked goods, desserts and confectionary.

properties.name: Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Co Ltd.
properties.about (Forest 500):
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the manufacture of a variety of paper products, including art paper, liquid packaging board, paying card, newsprint and copier paper. On top of its principal activities, making and selling paper products, the company also provides electricity, chemicals for paper manufacturing and construction materials. For example, through its subsidiaries Shandong Chenming Panels Co Ltd and Shouguang Chenming Floor Board Co Ltd, the company manufactures engineered wood products, including high-density fibreboard and wood flooring.
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd has manufacturing facilities located throughout China and distributes its products both domestically and to the international market, with overseas sales offices worldwide; in Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Brazil, and in Europe, India and Africa.  It is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies globally, ranking among the top 50, and as the second largest in China. The company produces around four million tonnes of paper products annually and until 2012 relied mostly on purchased chips and recovered fibre as the raw materials for its products. The company has since become increasingly integrated, developing a production base of plantation forests in China.

The group's agricultural business operates about 480,000 hectares of palm oil plantation as of 2016 and has one of the five largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. It also has an annual processing capacity of more than 12 million fresh fruit bunches and is one of the largest importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia. Its products include cooking oil and margarine. Additionally, the group crushes soya, with an annual capacity of 2.3 million metric tons. Sinar Mas is also a major pulp and paper producer with its company Asia Pulp and Paper, having an annual capacity of more than 20 million metric tons across its mills in Indonesia and China.

properties.name: Starbucks Corporation
properties.about (Forest 500):
The first Starbucks coffee store opened in 1971 in Seattle US. Over the next two decades the company expanded across the US and it completed its initial public offering in 1992. Since then the coffee chain has grown dramatically, opening its first non-North American stores in Japan and Singapore in 1996. As well as organic growth, Starbucks has acquired other cafe and beverage companies and even a music company. In 2013, Starbucks had over 3 billion customer visits to its 19,000 plus stores operating in 62 countries across the globe.  Growth has continued with the company moving into a further three countries and expanding its portfolio to over 21,000 outlets.
As well as roasting, marketing and selling coffee, Starbucks also sells tea products, juices, pastries, sandwiches, salads and beverage making equipment. Products are sold through company operated stores, licensed stores, grocery stores, national food service accounts and some franchised stores.
In addition to its major Starbucks brand the company also operates: Seattles Best Coffee, Teavana, Tazo, Evolution Fresh, La Boulange (bakery brand) and Torrefazione Italia Coffee. Starbucks is the largest cafe/bar owner in the world with revenues of $14.9bn. Starbucks uses paper in its packaging, soya (in milk) and palm oil (in its food products).

Target Corporation is a general merchandise retailer operating in the US. Established in 1902 and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, it is one of North America's retail giants, ranking among the top fifty in the Fortune 500. Target offers a variety of products including: food, beauty and personal care items; cleaning and paper products; as well as apparel and furniture, among other products. The company operates over 1,792 stores in the US as well as 38 distribution centres. Target began operating stores in Canada in 2011 through the acquisition of Zellers; however in 2015 the company planned to discontinue operating stores in the country.
A significant component of Target's sales are made up of its owned and exclusive branded products, which account for around one third of the company's total sales. Its owned branded products include: Archers Farms groceries; luggage; travel accessories; furniture; other goods sold under the Embark brand; Smith & Hawken outdoor furniture; Sutton & Dodge meat products; and up & up health and beauty products.

properties.about (Forest 500): Tesco started as a market stall in London in 1919, selling surplus groceries; its first store was opened ten years later in 1929. Following growth in the UK, Tesco floated on the London Stock Exchange in 1947. Today, Tesco is a multichannel grocery retailer active in eleven countries across Europe and Asia and also provides consumer financial services through its subsidiary, Tesco Bank. The company employs over 510,000 individuals and receives over 80 million shopping trips per week globally. In addition to its core grocery offering, in which it sells own branded and private label goods, Tesco sell a very broad range of other products including clothing, electronics, books and furniture. As a result of its large size and broad product range Tesco uses a range of forest risk commodities including, soy, beef, timber, paper and palm oil. In 2014, Tesco used 32,503 tons palm oil used in own brand products.

properties.name: Toyo Suisan Kaisha
properties.about (Forest 500):
Toyo Suisan Kaisha Ltd (Toyo) is an international food producer specialising in ramen noodles and seafood. Toyo manufactures its products through various sub-divisions, such as the Domestic Instant Noodles segment and the Frozen and Refrigerated Foods segment. In addition to noodles, it also produces wontons, soup products, fish, ham, sausages and seasonings. It also has a Prepared Food section which manufactures sterile packaged rice, retort rice, soup and other products.
The company was founded in 1953, has its headquarters in Tokyo, and employs around 4,600 people. Its main overseas operations are in Mexico and the Us through its Overseas Instant Noodles Division, which sells noodles under the brand name Maruchan Inc. As of 2008, Toyo owns three food processing facilities in the US and has 32 subsidiaries.
By the 1970s, Toyo had become well-known in Japan and had branched out internationally. It is now the largest noodle company in the US, the second largest in Japan and third largest in the world. It is also in the top five companies in Japan for dried processed food and chilled processed food, and in the top 30 largest soup companies worldwide.
The company does not appear to be a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm oil and in 2013 was implicated by the Rainforest Action Network to be one of the 'Snack Food 20' responsible for using 'conflict' palm oil from unsustainable sources,.

properties.name: Triputra Agro Persada
properties.about (Forest 500):
The Triputra Group is an Indonesian company, headquartered in Jakarta. The group is comprised of four main business segments: agribusiness, manufacturing, mining and, trading and services. Of most relevance are the company's operations in the production of agricultural commodities, which include rubber and palm oil. The group's subsidiary, Triputra Agro Persada (established in 2005) and its affiliates have a land bank of around 388,000 hectares and plan to increase this to 600,000 hectares by 2020.
Triputra Agro Persada began with the acquisition of PT Brahma Binabakti in Jambi province in Sumatra. In 2007, the company established a partnership with Union Sampoerna, marking the acquisition of 63,000 hectares of plantations in Central Kalimantan. The following year, in 2008, a partnership was formed with Yudha Group, further expanding the company's acreage with 20,000 hectares in East Kalimantan. The company continued to grow through other partnerships and with the support of a total of 13 national and international financial institutions, including ANZ, Bank Mandiri, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubushi and Rabobank. Triputra Agro Persada produced around 200,000 tons of crude palm oil in 2011 and employed around 24,000 people. It claims to be one of the largest oil palm companies in Indonesia.
PT Triputra Agro Persada is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO). In 2013 it reported to have 14,500 hectares of area under palm oil plantation and to have produced 90,000 MT of crude palm oil, 14,400 MT of palm kernel. It expects to achieve 100% certification of its estates by the end of 2015.

properties.name: Uni-President Enterprises
properties.sectors: Packaged food; Animal feed; Oils & fats; Food retail
properties.about (Forest 500):
Uni-President Enterprises Corp (UPEC) manufactures and distributes a range of food products through its network of 200 affiliate companies and convenience stores. The company was incorporated in 1967 in Tainan County, Taiwan. It was originally established as a rural flour factory but over the decades has grown into an international conglomerate with operations across Asia Pacific. The manufacturing of food products is one of the company's core businesses and although it has a wide range of interests, including sports teams, retail operations and pharmaceuticals, the manufacture of food and feed are the group's largest operations. Its main products include feeds, edible oils, soya sauce, meat products, instant noodles, dairy products and frozen foods, among others.
The manufacture and marketing of food and feed products are undertaken by five main groups. The Provisions Group manufactures and markets flour, fertilizer, eggs, and animal and aquatic feeds to Asian and other international markets. The Dairy and Beverage Group manufactures dairy products, teas, soft drinks, coffee and other beverages under brands such as €œPure Tea€, €œRae-Shie€ and €œLa Gauche de la Seine€.  In addition to Taiwan, the Dairy and Beverage Group operates in mainland China, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines. Edible oils and instant noodles are produced by the Instant Food Group, which has a 50% market share of Taiwan's instant noodle market. Instant products are also sold outside of Taiwan with products available in 30 countries across five continents. Brands include Unif, Imperial, One More Cup, Kikkoman, A-HA, Juicymart and Pure Tea. The two smallest Groups are the General Foods and Health groups. The former provides meat products, ice cream, sauces and ready meals while the Health Group manufactures bakery and health products,.
Of particular relevance is President Nisshin Corp, a member of Uni-President that supplies oils and fats, including palm oil products, to the food industry. Furthermore, palm oil is also used in other products, for example in instant noodles, and is sourced from Indonesia and Malaysia, while soya, imported from both the US and South America, is used in Uni-President's feed and edible oil products.

properties.name: VF Corp
properties.about (Forest 500):
VF Corp (VF) is a US-based global apparel company, manufacturing and supplying apparel, footwear and accessories. Headquartered in North Carolina, in the US, VF's products are sold in more than 150 countries worldwide, through 47,000 retail outlets and 1,100 of the company's own stores.
Its products are marketed principally under the company's own brands, within five business divisions: Outdoor and Action Sports, Jeanswear, Imagewear, Sportswear and Contemporary Brands. VF has a diverse portfolio of brands, including well-known names, such as outdoor apparel brand, The North Face, footwear, apparel and accessories brand, Timberland, and luggage and bag brands, Eastpak, JanSport and Kipling. The company produces around 450 million items per year, and operates manufacturing facilities in the Middle East, Europe, Mexico, and Central and South America. As these facilities meet only a proportion of the company's production needs, especially for the company's footwear production, VF sources products from around 1,900 independently and company-run facilities. VF sources raw materials, including leather, from multiple international suppliers.
VF Corp is a leader in the global bags and luggage market, ranking in the top ten globally and occupying a leading position in the US, where it ranks third by market share. It is also a top player in the more fragmented footwear industry, ranking as the third largest in the US by market share, and where it also holds the third position, and is in the top ten globally.

properties.name: Wolverine World Wide
properties.about (Forest 500):
Wolverine World Wide Inc (Wolverine) is one of the world's leading marketers of branded casual, active lifestyle, work, outdoor sport, athletic, children's and uniform footwear and apparel. Wolverine owns a number of well-known brands, including Merrell, Sperry Top-Sider, Hush Puppies, Saucony, Wolverine, Keds, Stride Rite, Sebago, Cushe, Chaco, Bates, HYTEST and Soft Style. The company is also the licensee of other recognised brands, including Cat, Harley-Davidson and Patagonia. The company's products are sold by leading retailers in around 200 countries and territories. Wolverine also operates 463 retail stores through leases with various third-party landlords in the US, Canada and United Kingdom.
In addition to its footwear and apparel business, Wolverine markets pigskin leather through its Wolverine Leathers subsidiary. About 98% (based on pairs) of the company's footwear products are sourced from third-party suppliers located primarily in the Asia Pacific region. Until recently the rest came from company-owned sources in the US and the Dominican Republic but the latter was recently closed.
In October 2012, Wolverine acquired Collective Brands Inc. via a consortium that also includes Golden Gate Capital and Blum Capital Partners. Collective Brands is in itself a major player in the footwear industry (owning the Payless brand, amongst others); it is a very large footwear retailer with more than 4,400 stores in over 30 countries.

properties.name: Yakult Honsha Co. Ltd
properties.about (Forest 500):
Yakult Honsha Co Ltd (Yakult) is a Japanese company, established in 1935 and incorporated in 1955; it is involved in the manufacture and distribution of food and drink products. The company has three main business segments: Beverages and Food Manufacturing and Sale; Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing and Sale; and Others. The company's original and still most recognisable product is a probiotic fermented milk drink sold under the Yakult brand. This continues to be the company's main product, particularly in the overseas market, where average daily sales of Yakult products in early 2013 were over 22.5 million. However, aside from its fermented milk and yogurt products (which include the Joie, Sofuhl, and Purela, amongst others) Yakult also offers non-dairy beverages such as flavoured tea drinks and juices, a range of cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and food products, including noodles.
As of 2013, the company had around 79 subsidiaries and 18 associated companies. The company has overseas and domestic operations, with its operations outside of Japan starting in 1964, when its Taiwanese subsidiary was established. Since then, this has grown and the company is now active in more than 30 countries and regions worldwide, including in Europe, the US, Brazil, Mexico, China, South Korea, Hong Kong, Indonesia, and elsewhere in Asia.
Yakult is a significant player in the global packaged food market, demonstrated by its leading position in a variety of markets worldwide. For example, specifically, it ranks among the top three companies in the dairy products market in Japan, and among the top ten for the packaged food industry overall. It is also among the top five companies with the largest market shares in the South Korean noodle industry, and holds a similarly high market share in the market for noodles in the United States, and is in the top 25 companies in the world for the packaged food industry.

properties.name: Zen-Noh (JA Group)
properties.about (Forest 500):
The Japan Agricultural Cooperatives Group (JA Group) is an agricultural cooperative, established to support its members by selling their products rather than each of its members selling products independently. On top of this, JA Group provides its members with production materials and agrochemicals. The group is a politically powerful organisation and is comprised of almost ten million regular and associate members. 
The JA Group is made up of several constituent parts, including ZEN-NOH, which is the National Federation of Agricultural Cooperative Associations. ZEN-NOH manages the business and distribution operations of the JA Group and is responsible for the marketing and supply business side of the group. Of particular relevance, are ZEN-NOH's operations in the animal feed sector. Of the total 24 to 25 million tonnes of compound feed used per year in Japan, ZEN-NOH handles around 30%, making ZEN-NOH Japan's largest compound feed producer and one of the top ten in the world. Through its subsidiaries, ZEN-NOH imports large volumes of soya from overseas producers including Brazil, India and China for use in compound animal feeds.
Also of relevance, is the group's Daily Necessities business unit, through which ZEN-NOH and JA run around 800 A-Coop supermarkets. The stores sell clothing, food products and consumer durables, and prioritise goods produced by members and sell A-Coop branded goods. Currently there are around 1,300 A-Coop branded goods, which include packaged food and clothing.

properties.about (Forest 500): The Adidas Group is a footwear and sports apparel company operating in over 160 countries worldwide. Famous brands include Reebok, TaylorMade and Adidas itself. Processed leather is used in many of its footwear products. The group has one of the largest global brand shares for footwear retail in terms of global retail value. It is also one of the largest footwear retailers in Western Europe, China and Hong Kong, as well as placing among the top five in the US.
